summary.text: Susan Collins is the Republican U.S. Senator from Maine, first elected in 1996 and now in her fifth term. A native of Caribou, she worked for Sen. William Cohen, held Maine and federal appointive posts and was the Republican nominee for governor in 1994 before entering the Senate. She chairs the Senate Appropriations Committee and is on the November 3, 2026 ballot for a sixth term.

paragraphs.text: Susan Collins was born on December 7, 1952, in Caribou, Maine, one of six siblings raised by Pat and Don Collins. Her family runs a lumber business founded in 1844, and both of her parents served as mayor of Caribou.
She graduated from Caribou High School in 1971 and from St. Lawrence University, Phi Beta Kappa, in 1975.

Collins began working for Maine Rep. William Cohen in 1975 and stayed on his staff when he was elected to the Senate, rising to staff director of the Oversight of Government Management Subcommittee of the Committee on Governmental Affairs.

Gov. John McKernan appointed her Commissioner of the Maine Department of Professional and Financial Regulation in 1987, and President George H.W. Bush appointed her director of the Small Business Administration's New England regional office in 1992. Ballotpedia also lists her as a deputy state treasurer of Massachusetts before her election to the Senate.
In 1994 she became founding executive director of the Center for Family Business at Husson College, now Husson University.

That year Collins won an eight-way Republican primary on June 14 and became the first Maine woman to receive a party nomination for governor. On election night she conceded to the two front-runners, Angus King and Joseph Brennan, with her own tally in third place.

Collins was elected to the U.S. Senate in 1996, succeeding Cohen, and was re-elected in 2002, 2008, 2014 and 2020. Her Senate biography says she was the first Republican woman to win a fifth term and has cast more than 10,000 consecutive votes.
In the 2025-2026 session she chairs the Appropriations Committee and also serves on the Health, Education, Labor, and Pensions and Intelligence committees.
Her Senate biography says she is married to Thomas A. Daffron and lives in Bangor, Maine.
